facts.dose: TWO puffs when needed for wheeze or breathlessness
warnings: Your label and leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist.
Use with a spacer if you have one.
Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working. Do not use more often than advised.
Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.
get_help: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing or swelling of the face or lips.

conflicts.label: TWO puffs when needed for wheeze or breathlessness
conflicts.leaflet: Usual dose: ONE puff when needed. Adults may take up to 2 puffs if needed.

conflicts.label: Maximum 4 times in 24 hours
conflicts.leaflet: Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours

steps.text_en: Your label and leaflet say different things. Your label says 2 puffs. Your leaflet says the usual dose is 1 puff. It says adults may take up to 2 puffs if needed. Ask your pharmacist. Use it no more than 4 times in 24 hours. Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours. Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working. Do not use it more often than advised.
steps.picture_prompt: A pharmacist behind a counter looking at a medicine box label and a folded leaflet side by side, with a gentle stop hand symbol

steps.text_en: This is your Salbutamol inhaler. It is for wheeze or breathlessness. You breathe it in through your mouth.
steps.picture_prompt: A blue and grey pressurised inhaler with a spacer tube beside it on a plain table

steps.text_en: Take 2 puffs when you need it for wheeze or breathlessness. Use a spacer if you have one.
steps.picture_prompt: A person sitting calmly holding an inhaler fitted to a spacer, two small puff clouds drawn beside it

steps.text_en: Take the cap off your inhaler. Shake it well. Fit your inhaler into the spacer.
steps.picture_prompt: Two hands shaking an inhaler with the cap removed, then pushing it into the end of a spacer

steps.text_en: Breathe out gently. Put the spacer mouthpiece in your mouth. Close your lips round it.
steps.picture_prompt: A side view of a person with lips closed around a spacer mouthpiece, holding the inhaler upright

steps.text_en: Press your inhaler once. Breathe in slowly and deeply.
steps.picture_prompt: A person pressing the top of the inhaler with one finger while breathing in, a gentle mist inside the spacer

steps.text_en: Hold your breath for about 10 seconds. Wait about 30 seconds before your next puff.
steps.picture_prompt: A person with puffed cheeks holding their breath, a plain round clock with a quarter of the face shaded beside them

steps.text_en: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing. Call 999 if your face or lips swell.
steps.picture_prompt: A person holding a mobile phone to their ear, looking worried, with an ambulance drawn in the background
